newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA COMPLETES BIGGEST SELL-OFF WITH SODI DEAL.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA COMPLETES BIGGEST SELL-OFF WITH SODI DEAL.

text.p: The sale by Bulgaria's Privatisation Agency of 60 percent in soda ash producer Sodi to Belgian chemicals and drugs group Solvay SA for $160 million is Bulgaria's biggest sell-off so far.

"This is the biggest privatisation deal in Bulgaria," said Privatisation Agency director Alexander Sabotinov. "It is a proof of the firm commitment of the Bulgarian government to implementing effective structural reforms."
The remaining shares in Sodi will be offered to Bulgarian investors through the country's mass privatisation programme and to Sodi staff.

Francois Massart, Solvay's treasury and corporate finance director, said Italian anti-trust authorities cleared the purchase on April 10 after Solvay agreed to share Sodi's output capacity with Turkish glass and chemicals producer Sise Cam.
To reduce pressure on the Italian market Sise Cam will take 25 percent of Sodi's production.

Solvay is negotiating to sell on part of its stake to Sise Cam and the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD), Massart said. He said the EBRD was considering investing $40 million and Sise Cam $30 million.
Under the contract Solvay will invest $67 million in the next five years to increase dense soda ash capacity from 400,000 tonnes a year at present and on modernisation and environmental improvements.
With yearly capacity of 1.2 million tonnes of sodium carbonate -- used among other things in glass, detergents, water and fumes treatment -- Sodi is the world's largest synthetic soda ash plant.
Solvay and the Privatisation Agency also agreed on the long term supply of limestone and salt as raw material and of steam and electricity, as well as the use of Varna harbour.
Solvay said that through the acquisition it would gain access to emerging markets in the Balkans, the Middle East, and Central Asia.
